subject.title: Feat: Add Trivy SBOM and vulnerability scanning to Docker release

question: Should Docker release publishing add Trivy SBOM/SARIF scanning with security-events write permission and a fixed-critical vulnerability gate after the checkout and proof gaps are fixed?
rationale: The PR changes trusted release workflow execution, third-party scanner installation, Code Scanning permissions, and release-blocking policy, which requires release/security owner intent beyond line-level correctness.

options.title: Require owner approval and full proof
options.body: Fix the backfill checkout, attach redacted full Docker release logs and Trivy artifact/SARIF evidence for both GHCR and Docker Hub, then have a release/security owner approve the scanner, permissions, and gate.

options.title: Accept release-pipeline risk
options.body: A release/security owner can intentionally accept the scanner, permission, partial proof, and gate risks and own any release or backfill fallout.

options.title: Pause for release-security design
options.body: Pause or close this PR if Docker release scanning should be introduced through a broader owner-led release security plan.

recommendation.title: Require owner approval and full proof
recommendation.body: Fix the backfill checkout, attach redacted full Docker release logs and Trivy artifact/SARIF evidence for both GHCR and Docker Hub, then have a release/security owner approve the scanner, permissions, and gate.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Docker release workflow and release-control history make this the strongest available owner signal for the policy decision.
